properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: APEX ENERGY (PA) LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/29/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8173633
Permit API: 129-28930
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Salem Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/29/2024
Comments: On January 29, 2024, inspection conducted at the Fatur Well Pad in Salem Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow-up to IR 3700597, which was conducted by DEP WQS at OGI request. During this inspection, a pink oily substance with elevated conductivity was discovered on the ground next to the onsite GPU unit and within its secondary containment. Violations were issued as a result. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The access road and well pad appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 2 and 3). The compressor noted in IR 3700597 had rags remaining within its secondary containment, soaking up what appears to be a petroleum based substance (see photos 4 and 6). However, it is on the verge of overflowing (see photo 7). No elevated conductivity readings were gathered from this substance (see photo 8), and there did not appear to be any staining on the ground around it. The well head onsite (well 10H) was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 13 and 14). Pooling was observed on the ground around the well head, however this appeared to be snowmelt due to the low conductivity and lack of discoloration (see photo 15). A Hugill's dumpster was observed on the eastern side of the pad dripping a dark fluid onto the ground (see photo 16). Although this fluid was not elevated in conductivity, the DEP recommends that this is addressed by the operator and necessary remediations are conducted if this is a regulated substance. The pink oily fluid observed during the time of IR 3700597 remains in the GPU secondary containment. The conductivity of this substance read 15,990 Microsiemens at the time of inspection (see photo 18). The disconnected hose and pink tinted substance remains on the gravel behind the GPU unit. The conductivity of this substance and/or ground surface read 724 Microsiemens at the time of inspection (see photo 19). The gear lubricant container holding a substance of similar coloration remains adjacent to the GPU unit (see photo 20). What appears to be a pump attached to the GPU unit was observed to be completely frosted over at the time of inspection (see photo 21). What appears to be an additional pump in disuse was observed on the ground adjacent to the GPU unit. A background soil conductivity reading was taken at the edge of the woods adjacent to the eastern side of the pad, which read 155.5 Microsiemens. Of the five additional tanks and equipment placed in secondary containment onsite that were not previously noted (see photos 3, 9, 11, 12, and 22), three of them appeared to be holding rainwater at the time of inspection. This does not comply with 25 PA Code 78a64a, as they appear to be reduced in capacity by at least 10 percent at the time of inspection, increasing the likelihood of discharge to the ground in the event of a spill. The ERP and PPC plan were found in the mailbox attached to the Act 9 sign (see photos 24 and 25).The DEP recommended in IR 3700597 that the operator ensure the structural integrity of the all production equipment is sound and properly contain and dispose of any production related fluid in accordance with current regulations to prevent any future pollution events. The DEP also recommended in IR 3700597 that the operator assess the red tinted fluid observed on the ground near the GPU as well as inside of the containment and remediate any spills in accordance with current regulations.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that not all necessary corrective actions has been taken for site to comply with current regulations. Violations remain outstanding, additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of operator response.

Violation ID: 8211210
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/17/2024
Comments: On 12/17/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 45F and sunny. An Act 9 sign and well permits are visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Hydraulic fracturing activities remain ongoing onsite and are estimated to be completed near the end of next week. Equipment to support well stimulation remain onsite and all equipment which is required to be held in containment was observed in secondary containment structures (photos #2-6)This inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced fluids from secondary containment reported by Greylock on 12/13/2024 at 0245 hours (CTS #385788). The cause of the release was determined to be a hydraulic fracturing pump which leaked produced fluids that accumulated and overtopped from secondary containment; the release has been contained. Contaminated material was already removed and backfilled by my arrival onsite (photo #7). The soil in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at ~40us/cm. Standing fluids were observed near the area of the release and field measured for EC at ~1140us/cm. Two vacuum trucks for removing fluids have been stationed onsite and were sent to remove the fluids from this area. Greylock took corrective action after this release and rebuilt the entire containment berm and rig-matting system with an 18-inch wall for increased capacity and to prevent additional releases (photo #8).The low points of the produced fluids offload containment structure which was the site of the release on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) have been repaired and a pump has been installed to continuously remove fluids from this containment structure as they accumulate (photos #9-11).The drainage system which was conveying fluids and diesel into the site's infiltration basin on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) remains shut in and a pump has been installed to remove accumulating fluids. No fluids were observed entering the basin at the time of this inspection (photo #12). Contaminated materials have not yet been excavated from the basin as per my previous recommendation to follow Act 2 remediation guidelines (photo #13).The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to remove fluids as they accumulate in secondary containment structures.-Continue following Act 2 remediation requirements for the ongoing remediation efforts onsite, including those set to take place in the infiltration basin.-Continuing daily secondary containment inspection.No additional violations noted at this time. The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Permit API: 059-27910
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Greene Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-02-18
Comments: On 02/14/2020 WQS Kristof Eichenlaub conducted incident response inspection # 2999089 On 02/18/2020 at approximately 1350 I conducted a follow up inspection at the site. Foamer product and sediment laden water were discharging from the sediment basin outlet, overwhelming two silt socks, and discharging outside the LOD into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. The discharge caused accelerated erosion below the silt socks and extending into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A contractor for Greylock was utilizing a bucket and a pressurized sprayer bottle in an attempt to remove foamer product from the sediment basin rip rap outlet. I inquired what the contractor was utilizing to eliminate the foam. The contractor informed me they were utilizing fabric softener. I contacted Greylock Regulatory Compliance Coordinator Keith Eighmey via phone, who indicated he was unaware of the contractor's activities. Eighmey indicated Greylock had previously utilized a defoaming agent in the channels and basin to eliminate foamer product. Eighmey indicated Greylock could provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The Department requests Greylock provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The spill had not been remediated and was continuing to discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A sediment laden water discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run was also continuing. Greylock discharged an additional substance to Waters of the Commonwealth during their attempt to remove the foamer. Some violations are ongoing as a result of a spill that was documented on 02/14/2020 (inspection # 2999089). Additional violations of CSL 301 and 307 have occurred due to Greylock discharging a chemical to UNT 8 to reduce the surfactant foam. A violation of OGA3259(2I) has occurred for failure to comply with DEP cleanup order issued on 02/14/2020.

Comments: On 3/18/21 at 1153 hrs., I conducted an inspection of DiversifiedProduction, LLC's F Kinter 3 well (API 063-35436) in Center Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a reported release of 42.5 barrels of production fluid onto the ground from a tank located onsite. According to the operator, corroded threads on a coupling connected to the tank was the cause of the release. Photos were submitted to the Department prior to inspection of the site. The release impacted the earthen berm containment area and a portion of an agricultural field to the north of the berm. Conductivity readings were elevated both within the earthen berm and outside the berm, indicating migration through the berm and soil in the adjacent field. The operator had tentatively delineated the northern extent of the migration with yellow flags. Soil conductivity beyond the northern most flag was at background level. The operator notified the Department that remediation of the site would commence on Monday, 3/22/21. The release of production fluids from a tank onto the ground constitutes violations of SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and 78.57(a). The violations associated with this release will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to Page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release and demonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to inspection 2995336 conducted on 2/10/2020 in which sediment laden storm water was observed leaving the operators access road and entering a stream. Only the portion of the access road where the discharge was occurring is being inspected. PADEP Eric Norman is assisting and Operator representative Isaac Haky is on site. The access road appears to have been regraded and CFS put down in several locations. While the regrading has abated the accelerated erosion rills observed in previous inspections, the Department recommends that the operator stabilize the access road to prevent a reoccurrence. The operator appears to have laid down stone on the portion of the access road which was previously pooling water and no pooled water or discharges are observed at this time. Based on this observation the CSL violations will be closed as corrected/abated effective 3/2/2020. The operator has placed CFS on either side of the road with soil berms that do not appear to be stabilized. The Department recommends that the berms be stabilized or removed. Based on their proximity to water conveyances the possibility exists that in a stormwater event they could be washed off into WOTC. The Department also recommends that the operator install CFS per the E&S Manual detail 4-1. Based on this inspection the CSL violations will be closed as corrected/abated. No new violations will be issued for this inspection. A follow up inspection for the other outstanding violations will be scheduled for a later date.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 949211
Permit API: 015-23529
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wilmot Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2022
Comments: Chesapeake Appalachia (CHK) called in a release of produced fluid at 14:48 on 3/24/22. The release was found around 13:30 the same day. It was reported that at least 1 barrel of produced fluid was released from secondary containment. I arrived onsite on 3/25/22 and met with Aaron Stredny, CHK, and Creston. The fluid was released from and improperly sealed hatch on the temporary storage tank onsite. The fluid then leaked from secondary containment through a hole in the corner. A lease operator was onsite earlier in the morning and did not notice any issues. It is believed that the release occurred during the morning of 3/24/22 until its discovery around 13:30. When I arrived an area behind the tank was already excavated to a depth of 6-12 inches. I checked conductivity of puddles and soil with Creston. The soil and puddles to west were below 1000 microsiemens. Moving east from the excavated area toward the pad berm puddles and soil were elevated upto 7800 microsiemens in some areas. Additional soil and puddles were checked outside the pad along the fill slope and into the neighboring field. Results were below 500 microsiemens. The excavation will continue in the areas of elevated conductivity to the west and under the secondary containment. CHK is waiting for Mountain Energy to remove the temporary tank and containment in order to excavate the area. Before the tank is moved surrounding puddles will be removed. At least 3 tri-axle loads were excavated. It is requested that CHK perform remediation of the site according to the requirements of Act 2 and provide the requested information indicated in this inspection.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SCORPIO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/21/2023
Violation Code: 102.22(b)1 - SITE STABILIZATION – TEMPORARY STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to temporarily stabilize the site to protect it from accelerated erosion and sedimentation where cessation of earth disturbance activities exceeded 4 days.
Violation ID: 8166117
Permit API: 053-31042
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/21/2023
Comments: This site is in the process of being constructed for a conventional well. The template for the well site has been completed. The well site location and access road have not been stoned. There has been no drilling activity on site and the pit has not been dug. There was no activity on site during the time of the inspection. The drilling permit and Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) Plan were posted at the entrance of the location.The road leading to the well site location did not have culverts, sumps, or ditches installed as outlined in the E and S Plan. There were no temporary BMPs in place at the time of the inspection. Areas of earth disturbance associated with the construction of the well site location were not seeded and mulched.At the time of inspection, the site showed evidence of accelerated erosion. Sediment laden water was flowing parallel to the access road along the bottom slope of the constructed bank (pictured in Photo 1). The sediment laden water was ponding at the lowest point on the well site location (pictured in Photo 2). Stormwater and sediment from the well sites under construction up slope of Hastings SDT 47 OG Well were also contributing to the accelerated erosion at the site (pictured in Photo 3). Due to the volume of water, overflow from the low point was discharging off the site location (pictured in Photo 4). The sediment laden water was flowing through the woods directly discharging into Hastings Run (pictured in Photo 5). The operator, Steven Tachoir, was contacted over a voicemail to discuss the results of this inspection. He has been advised to install temporary BMPs to prevent accelerated erosion until the permanent BMPs can be installed in accordance with the E and S Plan. He has also been advised to seed and mulch the areas of earth disturbance associated with construction of the well. It has been proposed to the operator to meet on site to further discuss options for remediation. Follow up inspections will continue to occur until the work has been completed.

Comments: On 3/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Stoorza well site. It was 28 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. There were water/ice puddles from recent rain/snowfall on the pad surface. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.There were two wells staged for production. Both wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank had secondary containment. A gas compressor is on site but was not running during the inspection.Three piles of excavated material from the Chesapeake Grippo well site are temporarily being stored on location until being approved for disposal. Each pile was staged in plastic-lined secondary containment. I field tested water puddles and soil around the perimeter of each excavation pile with the following results: The highest reading was on the north side of the south pile which was from a 1' x 8' water puddle outside the edge of the secondary containment that field tested at 3.04 mS conductance. Other water puddles around the perimeter of the south pile field tested at 0.7 mS conductance or less. Water puddles on the east side and west side of the two north piles field tested at 0.5 mS conductance. Water puddles along the north side of the two north piles field tested at 0.4 mS conductance or less. Water puddles south of the northwest pile field tested at 0.5 mS conductance or less. There were no water puddles south of the northeast pile. I field tested the soil south of the northeast pile with results at 0.7 mS conductance or less.No violations were noted during the inspection.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3524618 for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface in proximity to stockpiles of contaminated excavated waste.The DEP recommends the following:1. Remove the piles of excavated material as soon as the waste is approved for disposal.2. After removing the piles of excavated materials and secondary containment, screen the site for possible contamination and clean/report as necessary.I left the site at 1130 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8227907
Permit API: 123-47902
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/03/2025
Comments: The R H Stevenson Lease 4 conventional well is the nearest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the R H Stevenson lease. The tank battery is situated within earthen containment and consists of an upper level containing two stock tanks, and a lower level containing two polyurethane tanks. The stock tanks are plumbed into PVC piping that extends along the rear of the upper level of the earthen containment until terminating into the first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level. The first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level is also equipped with additional PVC piping apparently for the purpose of either removing or depositing fluids into the tank in the lower level of containment. At the time of this inspection, standing pools of fluid present in the upper level of the containment were found to have specific conductance measuring 5,980 microSiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). It was observed that straw had been laid down beneath the PVC piping in the upper level of containment. Where the straw cover ends, fluid was found to be actively flowing from the upper level of containment to the lower level. No fluid was observed to be flowing through the PVC piping connecting the stock tanks to the polyurethane tank during the time of this inspection. Neither polyurethane stock tank was found to have a noticeable volume of fluids contained within them at the time of this inspection. Some accumulation of fluids and crude oil could be observed around the base of the polyurethane tanks in the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection. The flow of fluids from the upper level to the lower level of containment was not found to be accumulating nor increasing the accumulated volume of fluids and crude oil present at the bottom of the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection.Approximately 40 feet south of the lower level tank battery containment area, crude oil and production fluids emerged on the soil surface. This flow of fluids continues west and is visually impacted by crude oil for approximately 180 feet. From there, soils and standing fluid with elevated specific conductance continue for approximately 75 feet before reaching a culvert. A pool of fluid at the entrance of the culvert was found to have specific conductance measuring 6,820 uS/cm.From the culvert, the fluid continues southwest in the natural swale for approximately 115 feet before reaching a point at which the swale transitions to an unnamed tributary (UNT) stream of Jackson Run, with defined bed and banks. At this point, waters in the UNT had specific conductance measuring 5,510 uS/cm. Specific conductance of 2,750 uS/cm was observed in the waters of the UNT in the remaining approximately 180 foot stretch, at which point there is a confluence with a second UNT of Jackson Run. Immediately before the confluence, waters in the impacted stream with specific conductance of 1,923 uS/cm were observed. Approximately two feet downstream of the confluence at a point with coordinates 41.95555, -79.29740 was the apparent end of impact to the UNTs of Jackson Run, where waters in the stream had a measured specific conductance of 42.6 uS/cm.At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the well.On 04/04/25 I called and spoke with William Cenk and Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. Mr. Cenk and Mr. Miller agreed to meet with Department officials onsite next week. A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: On 8/28/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Orr 14 OG well in Washington Township, Fayette County.The inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, received on 8/25/2026.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The access road appears to be a multi-use road that is shared with additional Diversified well sites. Evidence of minor stormwater washout was observed in portions of the shared access road at the time of inspection. The well site is located within a forested agricultural area. Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed downslope of the well site. The area surrounding the well site is heavily saturated, with evidence of heavy animal traffic observable at the time of inspection. The E and S/Restoration plan was not located on site during this inspection. However, the E and S/Restoration plan was located during a Department SubSurface inspection (IR 4266229) that overlaps the time of this inspection.- The gas well is equipped with a well tag. No additional equipment related to well plugging and/or production was observed on site during this inspection. The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was not observed on site.- While on site, the Department spoke with Ed from Glade Pipeline Services, who confirmed that third-party disturbances are occurring at the well site due to livestock grazing, and explained that they were on site to make repairs on the access road and the well site.- Upon exiting the site toward Connellsville Street, the Department observed loose soil that had been pushed adjacent to an apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run during today's aforementioned access road repairs (Photos 17-20). Although no sediment was observed entering this apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run at the time of inspection, it is actively under threat by this site since no E and S control measures are installed in this location. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate action to cease ongoing threats to the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures prior to conducting earth disturbances on the access road, which is resulting in a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending review of the site E and S plan in a subsequent surface inspection.An additional violation will be issued in IR 4265922 for failure to post the Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) on site.While on site, the Department notified Diversified representative Daniel Frick via voicemail of the Department's observations and forthcoming violations from this inspection and IR 4265922.

Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/29/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report from the operator that an estimated 20 barrels of a fresh water and produced water mixture had been released to the surface of Pad B on the same day, 3/29/22. I met with EQT representative Rick Hall upon arriving on location. Mr. Hall stated that a frac tank had been overflowed with the produced water and fresh water mixture. He said the fluid had made its way outside of the secondary containment and into the travel lane and ditch along the southwest pad edge. There is a brush barrier alongside the ditch at the edge of the pad. No fluid was observed on the opposite side of the brush barrier. I took several electrical conductivity (EC) readings of the fluid on the pad surface and in the mud in the ditch. With the Oakton conductivity meter I measured an EC of >19.99 on the pad surface immediately next to the edge of the containment where the frac tanks are located. In the middle of the travel lane, I measured an EC of approximately 16 mS/cm. The mud in the ditch at the pad edge gave me an EC reading of approximately 14 mS/cm. Excavators were present on the pad in addition to roll-off boxes to contain excavated material. A Tobias construction crew began to excavate the affected pad material during this inspection. A Creston Environmental employee was also present conducting screening on the pad surface with a YSI meter. On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. No issues noted on Pad A. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation for the release on Pad B due to the estimated volume of the release. The Department requests a justification for the estimated spill volume. Violations noted.

Inspection Date: 6/24/2022
Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the COP Tract 551-B pad. Inspection accompanied by EQT Lead EHS Coordinator Mark Barbier. Meeting on site with EQT Company Man Mike Hood. Weather conditions at time of inspection are partly cloudy, humid and 73 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while EQT reviews SOPs.According to the Standard Detail Report, the spill notification was submitted by Mr. Barbier. At around 0800 hours, US Well Services was swabbing the well to switch over from the 6H to the 7H well. At that time, the open topped blender hopper overflowed releasing an estimated 140 barrels of fluid to containment, of which an unknown quantity of fluid overtopped the containment structures. During discussions on site with Mr. Barbier, the estimation was based on the fact that the pumps may have been releasing 20 barrels per minute for 7 minutes, although the exact volume can not be determined. The Department conducted conductivity screenings using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Pooled fluid remaining within the containment structure was observed with conductivity readings between 7-8 mS/cm. Fluid within the north pad ditch and sumps outside of containment ranged from 3.92-5.37 mS/cm. Visual evidence of spilled fluid extended from a brushy area at the north conrer of the pad, along the entire ditch perimeter into the woods at the eastern corner of the pad where appeared to collect in a row of silt sock. Two vac trucks are present on site. One truck is vacuuming fluid from containment, a second truck is pumping spilled fluid collecting at he low point in the eastern corner of the pad ditch (photo 9). Visual observations near the blender unit indicated that fluid was released with sufficient force to release frac sand from the hopper. Two drums of frac sand were hand shoveled from the spill area (photo 10). Friction reducer material was also observed on pad rock outside containment. On the pad surface, spilled fluid is observed leaking through pad rock under the working tank secondary containment (photo 5). Pad rock affected by spilled fluid under containment is estimated to cover an area of 250 feet in length by 25-40 feet in width. Comments: The DEP conducted a follow-up inspection on Seneca Resource's Covington Pad G (Pino Pad G) located in Covington Township, Tioga County on 10/20/2021 at 1035 hours. The weather was 63 degrees with clear skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release of ~30 gallons of produced water to the pad surface that occurred on 10/7/2021. Complaint Tracking System ID #359859 is tied to this release. On 10/7/2021, Seneca Resource's contacted the DEP spill reporting hotline to report that ~30 gallons of produced water had released to the pad surface after a wash-out had occurred on the produced water flow-line. Produced water was discovered to have been released from the flow-line at a point where insulation was wrapped around the line. Upon removing the insulation, a small spray of produced water covered an area approximately 20ft by 5ft in area. The impacted area was then screened and excavated to remediate the release. All excavated material was placed into residual waste containers to await proper disposal. Samples were collected to ensure remediation efforts were efficient. While onsite today, the area was observed (photo #2) and pooled water had filled the excavated pit. Water within the pit was field measured at ~920us/cm today. Other pooled water and soils in the direct surrounding area were all field measured below 1.0mS/cm. I spoke with a Seneca representative while onsite who explained that they are awaiting confirmatory sample results before backfilling occurs. I agreed with the plan and contacted Andy Woodward with Seneca Resources to confirm. Upon confirmatory sample results showing normal ranges, the area will be backfilled with clean fill. Based on the release of ~30 gallons of produced water to the pad surface and the timely remediation conducted by Seneca, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #117-20337: 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a) SWMA 301 CSL 402(b) I departed the site at 1130 hours.

An onsite meeting was scheduled with Petro Erie Inc. and the Department which developed this Inspection Report.Individuals present at the onsite meeting:Harry Rhoades -Owner/Operator of Petro Erie Inc.Chris Rhoades -Driver for Harry RhoadesRob Bechtel -PA DEPRick Willey -PA DEPAlan Wolf -PA DEPLucas Eichner -PA DEPSteve Wells -PA DEPThe meeting was started off by Rob Bechtel stating the reason for the meeting and what was discovered during a previous site inspection on 7/21/2023 with violations cited. It was discussed that there is a potential that the discharge of produced fluid from the tank battery may have impacted the Reno, PA public water supply. Mr. Rhoades asked if the pubic water supply was now safe to drink and if regular testing was being conducted. We informed him that the oil and gas program was collecting samples for analysis to determine if the water supply was impacted by oil and gas activity and that the Safe Drinking Water program was working with Venango Water Company related to the public water supply. The discussion with Mr. Rhoades made him aware of the fact that there are more than several concerns with his lease. The Department recommended that he hire an environmental consultant to help him through the cleanup and reporting process of an Act 2 cleanup regarding the discharge of produced fluid and the potential impact of the Reno public water supply. Other violations were discussed regarding the other wells on his lease. Violation ID: 8286045

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/19/2026
Comments: On August 19, 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the Cecil 2-P229 OG Well in regard to CTS 400392.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.At the time of the inspection the well was located in an open agricultural field. The access road appeared stabilized. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the production equipment, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag and well posting were present onsite appeared to have all information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). There were no observed leaks or discharges of fluid at the surface around the wellhead.There appeared to be 3 total production tanks onsite. Upon further inspection, it appeared the white poly tank was connected and in use. The tank appeared to be in sound condition with no observed leaks or discharges of fluid were observed around this tank.Two metal tanks were also present onsite but did not appear to be in use at the time of the inspection. Upon further inspection of the 2 metal tanks, one of the tanks appeared to be severely corroded with multiple holes in the tank observed. The Department observed fluid flowing down the side of the tank. A conductivity reading of this fluid was obtained and was "OR" (Over detectable range, >20mS). Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Violation ID: 999888
Permit API: 015-21707
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Franklin Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/28/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Chesapeake's "Sensinger" Marcellus well site.Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake) called the DEP yesterday (June 27, 2023) to report an estimated 20 barrel release of production liquid to the pad surface.I spoke with Eric Hottenstein by phone during this inspection. He explained the following: on June 18, 2023 a vac truck was removing liquid from the production tank. Apparently when the truck left, the valve on the tank was not fully closed, and the camlock plug did not seal. Yesterday Chesapeake's Well Tender saw liquid dripping from the yellow takeout can attached to the production tank. They were immediately able to get the leak to stop. The detection system on the production tank indicates that 20 barrels of production liquid leaked out of the takeout can during the ~10 days it was leaking. Creston Environmental obtained electrical conductivity readings from soil around the tank which indicated contamination from the leak. Hottenstein also explained the Marcellus well at this site produces Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material (NORM). I used a Ludlum 2241-3 meter with a scintillator probe to detect radioactivity. Background reading was 10 uR/hr. Readings ~1" from the production tank were 50-70 uR/hr. Chesapeake contracted Waste Management to decontaminate the production tank. They plan to remove the tank after decon on Monday July 3, 2023. Excavation of contaminated pad material will commence after tank removal. The production liquid release apparently infiltrated into the pad material around/under the tank. Vegetation immediately surrounding the production tank appears stressed (brown) from the leak. I used a Hanna Groline soil probe to get electrical conductivity readings from pad material surrounding the tank. The meter maxed out at 4.0 mS/cm, indicating contamination from the production liquid.Violations for the production liquid release are cited to the 015-21707 drilling permit. Due to the quantity of the release, cleanup is referred to DEP's Environmental Brownfields Program.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water on the pad surface in 4 separate puddles has electrical conductivity of 0.21-1.3 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.Air temp 67FJLP

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Seneca Resource's Dandois 482 well site located in Sullivan Township, Tioga County on 5/3/2024 at 1100 hours. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID # 380387 is tied to this release within CTS.Seneca Resource's reported to the DEP reporting hotline that on 5/2/2024 at ~2300 hours a produced water dump line washed out and caused a release of approximately 10 gallons of produced water to the pad surface (photos #1 and 2). They planned to utilized a hydrovac truck (which was already onsite) to perform the majority of the clean-up around the pipes. A Seneca Resources representative onsite provided me with photos after remediation was completed (photos #4-6). The area has already been backfilled.Based on the reported release and Seneca Resource's timely remediation of the release, violations of the following are cited against API #117-20558 as immediately corrected at this time:25 Pa. Report Details

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 845527
Permit API: 129-25936
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Fairfield Twp

Inspection Date: 2019-03-28
Comments: Inspection record #2860077 submitted on 3-28-19 was submitted in error. This inspection supersedes inspection record #2860077. At time of inspection well appears equipped for production. Department observes a thick, light yellow substance coming from brine tank. This substance appears to be petroleum based. This substance appears to be leaking from the top of the brine tank, where the piping from the well head attaches. This substance flows down the side of the brine tank (photo #1), and has ponded in two areas at the base of the brine tank (photo #2). Department contacted operator rep Josh Martz by phone from site. Mr. Martz states a well tender will be sent to the site. 14:42- Mr. Martz contacted Department by phone, left message. Mr. Martz states a release of approx 5-6 gal of crude oil occurred. Mr. Martz states water forced the tank to overflow. Mr. Martz states the tank has been emptied of water and that he will report the release to the DEP emergency line. 14:59- Department received spill report. This report states 5-6 gal of crude oil was released on 3-28-19. 16:32- Mr. Martz contacted Department by phone, left message. Mr. Martz states surface clean up has been completed. Mr. Martz states the crude oil will be removed from the tank next week. Mr. Martz states after crude oil is removed, the tank will be cleaned up, impacted soil will be removed, area under tank will be checked and impacted soil, if any, removed. Mr. Martz also states he will provide photos of cleanup to Department and will keep Department updated on status of site. Violations are being issued for failure to collect brine or other fluids, failure to control and dispose of fluids, and for disposal of residual waste inconsistent with the rules and regulations of DEP. A follow up inspection will be conducted at a later date.

Violation ID: 8276187

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/26/2026
Comments: On 5/26/2026, the Department conducted an at the former location of the Holchin 2 well site in North Union Township, Fayette County. This inspection follows-up to IR 4181294, where no Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) was installed at the site entrance per the Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan. In response, violations were issued for failure to failure to follow the E and S plan.An NOV Response to IR 4181294 was requested from the operator by 4/30/2026. However, no response of any kind to IR 4181294 has been received from the operator at the time of this inspection. The Department issued an Order to Diversified (#445705) on August 15, 2025. According to the Order, Diversified is to restore the Well Sites within nine (9) months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/08/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 1/08/2027 in accordance with current regulations.The following was observed during the inspection:A well plugging monument with the API number displayed was observed in the former location of the gas well (photos 19 and 20). No evidence of a spill to the surface, such as staining, was observed at the former well site location. No equipment related to well plugging and/or production was observed on site during this inspection. No evidence of nuisance mud tracking was observed from the site entrance onto Cutler Road (photo 1). The former access road and well site are temporarily stabilized and have established some vegetative growth since the time of IR 4181294, exhibiting approximately 40% vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. However, the third-party disturbances identified in IR 4181294 due livestock grazing continue to occur on site. The Department continues to recommend that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. Temporary Erosion and sedimentation controls are installed downslope of the access road (photo 10). An access road cross-culvert is also protected by Compost Filter Sock (CFS). (photo 13) The site E and S/Restoration plans are available in a mailbox on site (photos 4-6). No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation due to well plugging operations was observed on site during this inspection. However, some areas downslope of the former well site appear to lack the temporary E and S controls shown on the E and S plan drawing. Therefore, it appears that the operator continues to fail to follow the E and S control plan. Based on observations from this inspection, the violations issued in IR 4181294 shall remain outstanding. The Department recommends continued seeding and temporary stabilization on site until 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage is achieved. The violation issued in IR 4177612 for failure to post the API number on site shall be closed in IR 4205025.

Comments: Weather was 65° and sunny at time of inspection. Met with Seneca representatives Glenn Heckman and Trey Porter on location. Inspection was being conducted for the conclusion of a 72 hour Pressure build up test (PBT) that began on 9/16/19. Clayton Shucker and Kyle Jackson were on location from Moody and Associates Inc. (Moody's) to collect isotopic samples if possible from the 3 annular spaces that were closed in for the PBT. The 3 annular spaces that were tested were the 20x13, 13x9 and 9x5. The 20x13 had a reading of -5 psi, 13x9 was -3 psi and the 9x5 was 150 psi. For the 20x13 annular space Moodys detected 100% LEL and 86% methane by volume and was able to grab a sample. That sample depleted the gas that was trapped in the annular space and I was unable to sample it. For the 13x9 vent Moody's detected 100% LEL and 7% methane but there was an insufficient volume of gas present to sample the annular space. The 9x5 space had 100% LEL and 100% methane detected. Moodys grabbed a sample and I grabbed a sample for isotopic analysis. The well was then opened up for Nine Energy Services to run temperature and acoustic gradient logs. Trey Porter is to send a follow up at the conclusion of the temperature and audio logs since they were running well into the evening to complete them. No new violations were cited at time of inspection.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/03/2025 to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Kingsley Township, Forest county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/03/2025
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8254677
Permit API: 053-31182
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Kingsley Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/03/2025
Comments: This conventional well was actively being fractured at the time of this inspection. The drilling permit and E and S Plan were posted at the entrance of the location. The access road and well site location are stoned, but due to the recent heavy traffic the road surface and site are losing their shape and stability. The road and site should be reshaped and additional clean stone considered to provide a durable road surface for continued well development on the Clinger lease. Gathering lines have been installed and backfilled within the road ditch up to this well site. Rather than grading and shaping the road ditch after the pipeline install, the backfilled material is mounded and un-stabilized. This loose fill material is at high risk for accelerated erosion and sedimentation during a rain event and is acting as a barrier for stormwater conveyance in the road ditch. The fill material within the ditch should be compacted or removed and the ditch is expected to be properly defined and temporarily stabilized in order for the ditch to function properly. The road banks and the disturbed areas around the perimeter of the well location have not been properly graded or temporarily stabilized. The road banks greatly exceed a 3:1 slope in several areas and are therefore sloughing significantly. These areas will need to be re-graded and temporarily stabilized to meet the requirements of the Chapter 102 regulations. The culvert northeast of the well location has still not been installed. Several of the culverts installed on the nearby access roads have also not been installed in accordance with the E and S Plan. The inlets of several of the culverts are plugged with fill material due to the sloughing, un-stabilized banks. The sediment plugging the culverts will need to be removed in order for them to function properly. According to the E and S Plan, stone rip-rap is expected to be placed at and below the outlet of the culvert pipes to dissipate the outfall. Infiltration berms should be installed beyond the outlet of the culverts. Several of the culvert outlets that were installed on the lease are directing stormwater towards un-stabilized fill material from the construction of the road. None of the outlets have stone rip-rap or an infiltration berm to dissipate the outfall of stormwater. These concerns will need to be addressed as outlined in the E and S Plan to meet the requirements of the Chapter 102 regulations.A follow up inspection will be conducted to ensure the above concerns have been addressed properly and in a timely manner. Due to the risk of pollution via accelerated erosion and sedimentation it is highly recommended to address these concerns prior to the next rain event.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/26/2026 to EQT ARO LLC in Noyes Township, Clinton county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/26/2026
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8268424
Permit API: 035-21178
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Noyes Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/26/2026
Comments: On March 26, 2026, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident site inspection at the EQT ARO LLC COP Tract 343 Pad C. On March 25, 2026, at 1526, EQT reported a spill of drilling mud outside of containment onto the well pad surface to the DEP spill hotline. Coastal Rig 103 is onsite conducting plugging operations on the C1015H Well. The plugging rig had moved onsite on Monday, March 23, 2026. Prior to the plugging rig being onsite a snubbing rig was located onsite. When the plugging rig mobilized to the site, large water puddles from recent rain covered some of the well pad. Once the puddles dried, an area approximately 40 feet by 20 feet was noticed to the north of the rig containment. DEP spoke with Tobias Excavating and he said that last evening he tested the impacted area with a PID meter and did not return elevated results on the meter. Tobias said Matt Locke with Tuscarora Geologic and Environmental Services screened the area last evening with a conductivity meter and did not return elevated results on the meter. DEP spoke with EQT Rick Hall on the phone while onsite and EQT thinks drilling mud was sprayed while the snubbing rig was onsite and the spill did not reveal itself until the water onsite dried up. Mr. Hall estimates approximately 25 gallons of drilling mud was spilled outside of containment onto the well pad surface. At the time of inspection, Tobias had already scraped up the impacted area and placed the impacted soil into rolloff dumpsters. Approximately, an inch to three inches of stone and soil were scraped up to remove the impacted material. While conducting the inspection, Tobias was spreading top stone on the area that was scraped up. The spilling of drilling mud outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Due to the immediate response to clean up the spill the violations are consider to be immediately corrected.
